definitions.explanation: Used to describe fresh, perishable food products, particularly produce, meat, and seafood.

examples.japanese: {生鮮|せいせん}{食品|しょくひん}コーナーで{買|か}い{物|もの}をする。
examples.english: I shop in the fresh food section.

examples.japanese: {生鮮|せいせん}{野菜|やさい}は{早|はや}く{食|た}べた{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: Fresh vegetables should be eaten quickly.

examples.japanese: {生鮮|せいせん}{市場|いちば}で{魚|さかな}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought fish at the fresh food market.

notes:
{生鮮|せいせん} is a no-adjective meaning fresh, specifically for perishable food products.

WORD FORMATION:
{生|せい} (raw, fresh) + {鮮|せん} (fresh, vivid) = fresh (food)

GRAMMAR:
Used as no-adjective before nouns: {生鮮|せいせん}{食品|しょくひん} (fresh food)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生鮮|せいせん}{食品|しょくひん}: fresh food, perishables
- {生鮮|せいせん}{野菜|やさい}: fresh vegetables
- {生鮮|せいせん}{魚介|ぎょかい}: fresh seafood
- {生鮮|せいせん}{肉|にく}: fresh meat
- {生鮮|せいせん}{市場|いちば}: fresh food market
- {生鮮|せいせん}コーナー/{売|う}り{場|ば}: fresh food section

SUPERMARKET SECTIONS:
- {生鮮|せいせん}{食品|しょくひん}: fresh section (vegetables, meat, fish)
- {加工|かこう}{食品|しょくひん}: processed foods
- {冷凍|れいとう}{食品|しょくひん}: frozen foods
- {日配|にっぱい}{品|ひん}: daily delivered items (dairy, bread)

NUANCE:
{生鮮|せいせん} specifically refers to perishable freshness (needing refrigeration), while {新鮮|しんせん} is broader "freshness" including experiences and ideas.
